# Persist ledger entries in a local SQLite store

Pocket Ledger keeps every transaction in a single-file SQLite database so the CLI
works fully offline and a backup is a plain file copy. This ticket lands the store
module and its schema; everything downstream reads through it rather than touching
`sqlite3` directly.

## Scope

- Create the `entries` table with a monotonic `id`, an ISO-8601 `booked_at`, a
  signed integer `amount_cents`, and a free-text `memo`.
- Expose `append(entry)` and `iter_range(start, end)` on a `LedgerStore` class.
- Open the database in WAL mode so reads never block the single writer.

## Schema

| Column        | Type    | Notes                                  |
| ------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | INTEGER | Primary key, autoincrement             |
| `booked_at`   | TEXT    | ISO-8601, UTC, indexed for range scans |
| `amount_cents`| INTEGER | Signed; debits negative[^cents]        |
| `memo`        | TEXT    | Optional, trimmed on write             |

[^cents]: Amounts are stored as integer cents to avoid binary floating-point drift
    on sums; formatting to a decimal happens only at the presentation edge.

## Reference usage

```python
from pocket_ledger.store.sqlite import LedgerStore

store = LedgerStore.open("~/.pocket-ledger/ledger.db")
store.append(Entry(booked_at="2026-02-01T09:30:00Z", amount_cents=-1299, memo="coffee"))
for entry in store.iter_range("2026-02-01", "2026-03-01"):
    print(entry.memo, entry.amount_cents)
```
